claim_en: HORIDUHU elai ('BRING HIM DOWN to me'): the form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — and its partner is the wound itself: 'and Potiphar bought him... from the hand of the Ishmaelites who BROUGHT HIM DOWN there' (Gen 39:1). The brother sold down and the brother demanded down share one skeleton; the Ramah rules both spellings letter-identical (full vav before the resh, lean yod before the dalet, lean final vav).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 44:16 (the Masorah's three dageshed)
claim_en: HINENU avadim ('HERE WE ARE, my lord's slaves'): both nuns dageshed, the first vowel segol — the Masorah counts THREE such in the Torah and the census is exact: the surrender at the cup (44:16), the brothers' final 'here we are, your slaves' (Gen 50:18), and the doomed climbers' 'here we are, we will go up' (Num 14:40): three offered selves, each refused (the dagesh checked in-stream at the first station).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 44:15 (the Ramah; an old scroll-correction's variant locked out)
claim_en: ish asher KAMONI ('a man LIKE ME'): written LEAN (no vav) — the whole Torah so, per the Masorah and the Ramah against a scroll-correction's full variant — and the lean form stands exactly THREE times: the masked governor's divination-claim (44:15), the Holy One's plague-word 'there is none LIKE ME in all the earth' (Exod 9:14), and the prophet 'LIKE ME' whom Moses promises (Deut 18:15): a mask, the Name, and the prophet in one lean skeleton.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 44:18 (the Masorah)
claim_en: VE-AL YICHAR apekha ('and let not your anger burn'): the phrase stands exactly TWICE in the Torah, BOTH in this cycle — Judah's plea before the speech (44:18) and Joseph's own pardon-sentence 'let it not burn in your eyes that you sold me here' (45:5): the plea against anger, and the absolution of it, two chapters apart.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 44:20 (the Masorah)
claim_en: One verse carries TWO pair-words: VE-YELED ('and a child') — twice in the Torah: the child of old age (44:20) and Lemech's 'a CHILD for my wound' (Gen 4:23, the Kitzur reading the wound forward); and VE-YOTER ('and he was left') — twice: 'and Jacob was LEFT alone' at the wrestling (32:25, asserted) and Benjamin 'LEFT alone of his mother' (44:20): the wounded child and the father's own alone, both in the son's plea.

source: Minchat Shai + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 44:29
claim_en: VE-HORADTEM ('and you will bring down'): THREE tokens in the Torah — the father's dread twice ('my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol', 42:38; 'in evil to Sheol', 44:29) and the sons' JOY-command one chapter ahead: 'bring my father DOWN here' (45:13): the verb that buries is the verb that reunites; the Kitzur's cow-and-calf parable named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 44:11 (the Ramah; the Masorah)
claim_en: VA-YORIDU ('and they lowered'): full vav before the resh, lean yod before the dalet — exactly TWICE in the Torah: the bags lowered for the search (44:11) and the spies' fruit 'brought down to us' (Deut 1:25); an old scroll-correction's shorter variant is locked out by the Masorah's own two-token note: both descents carry evidence.

VA-YASIGEM ('and he overtook them'): written LEAN — its one such token, against the rule MS states: every hiriq-pointed form of this word in the Torah is written full yod; the pursuit itself is clipped.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 44:10 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi copies)
claim_en: NEQIYIM ('clean' — the steward clearing the nine): written with ONE yod — the Hilleli one yod, the Yerushalmi two, and all our books one; MS untangles the Great Masorah's own confused three-lean note (its sign belongs to another language-family): the one-yod clean stands once so here.

KI-ROTO ('when he sees'): FULL with the Hilleli copy and every book — and MS corrects the Great Masorah's SWAPPED note (it called the later token full: backwards — the lean partner is Josiah's death-verse, 2 Kgs 23:29, named). In the same file: TISFUN ('you shall not again', 44:23) lean vav lean yod with all books and the Hilleli (its Deuteronomy partner named, asserted).

The dismissal-verse wears two rare strokes: HA-ISH ('the man') under the PAZER (MS's ruling names the great pazer; SNAPSHOT writes the pazer stroke in-stream — the naming question between the pazer and its great form is carried named, not merged) and HU ('he') under the YETIV stroke (asserted): the verse that frees the nine is the span's most heavily marked.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 44:30 (the Masorah)
claim_en: ve-nafsho QESHURA ve-nafsho ('and his soul is BOUND to his soul'): the bound-word stands ONCE in the Torah; Scripture's pair is 'folly bound in the heart of a lad' (Prov 22:15, named) — the Kitzur reads the lad's folly against the father's love, and the binding holds either way.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 44:2/9/10/15/18/23 (the chapter's file); Mikhlol
claim_en: The chapter's pointing file: ha-QATAN ('the youngest', 44:23) with the qof DAGESHED (checked); gevii ('my cup', 44:2) with no restraining-stroke on the vav, VE-GAM ('and also', 44:9) keeping its vav against erring readers and copies, ki-dvrekhem ('according to your words', 44:10) kaf soft (Mikhlol), halo yedatem ('did you not know', 44:15) full per the Shelach list, dvar ('a word', 44:18) dalet soft — all asserted; named: the closed portion-break at va-yigash (44:18), the seam standing at Judah's step forward.

THIS UNIT'S VERSE IS THE TRADITION'S OWN TYPE-SPECIMEN FOR THE INFERENCE RULE THE MACHINE CITES EVERYWHERE, AND THE INK BACKS THE CHOICE. R. Yishmael teaches that ten arguments from the lesser to the greater ‹קַל וָחֹמֶר› ('kal va-ḥomer') are written in Scripture, and the census OPENS with 44:8 - 'the silver we found we returned to you; how then should we steal?' - continuing through Moses' 'the children of Israel did not heed me, how then will Pharaoh,' the spittle and the seven days, 'while I yet live you are defiant - how much more after my death,' and six more. Machine-checked on the Torah members: the two-particle frame the first two share, BEHOLD followed by AND HOW, stands at exactly THREE Torah verses - 44:8, the Exodus verse the census names, and that verse's own restatement eight verses later. The particle 'and how' alone stands at five seats. The census's opening pair is not an arbitrary selection: it is the whole Torah population of the form, less one repetition.

THE TRANSLATION REFUSES TO LET THE RIGHTEOUS ONE PRACTICE WHAT THE TORAH FORBIDS, AND THE WORD'S ONLY OTHER SEAT IS THE PROHIBITION ITSELF. Where the steward's charge and Joseph's boast both use ‹נַחֵשׁ יְנַחֵשׁ› ('naḥesh yenaḥesh,' he surely divines), Onkelos writes at both seats that he thoroughly INVESTIGATES ‹בָּדָקָא מְבָדֵק› ('badaka mevadek') - the goblet converted from an oracle into an instrument of inquiry. Machine-checked across the whole Torah: the divination root in this form stands at exactly FIVE tokens across THREE verses - twice at 44:5, twice at 44:15, and ONCE MORE at Deuteronomy 18:10, which is the verse that FORBIDS divination. The word has no other home in the corpus. The translation's buffer is therefore not squeamishness: the only other place the Torah uses this word, it outlaws the practice.

A DOUBLED PHRASE STANDS AT EXACTLY TWO SEATS IN THE TORAH, SEVEN CHAPTERS APART, AND THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BOTH THE SAME WAY. When Jacob quotes himself - 'surely he is TORN, TORN ‹טָרֹף טֹרָף› (tarof toraf)' - Onkelos writes surely he is KILLED, the identical rendering this corpus recorded at the original scene. Machine-checked: the doubled pair stands at exactly TWO Torah seats, 37:33 and 44:28, both about the same son; the only other occurrence of the first word anywhere in the Torah is followed by a different form, in the herdsman's law. The translation's verdict on the beast-death holds when the same words are re-spoken seven chapters later - and the standing confrontation dossier has Joseph throwing that very phrase back at them.

ONE SPEECH IS HELD TO DISCHARGE THREE SEPARATE ESTRANGEMENTS AT ONCE, AND THE RISK IT RAN IS DISPUTED. R. Ḥiyya bar Abba reads everything Judah says from 44:18 until 'Joseph could not restrain himself' as conciliation three ways simultaneously - toward Joseph (see how he gives his life for Rachel's son, the very brother he once sold), toward the brothers (see how he gives his life for a brother), and toward Benjamin (as I give my life for you, so would I for your brother). The repentance the sale has been waiting on, delivered in a single argument. Carried with its recorded dispute on what follows: one master holds Joseph did NOT act properly in clearing the room, since one kick would have killed him; another holds he acted properly, knowing his brothers were not suspected of bloodshed.

check.note: A single speech read as discharging three distinct estrangements at once, carried with a recorded dispute over the risk of the response.

claim_en: PERSUASION IS MODELLED AS INCREMENTAL EXTRACTION, KNOT BY KNOT. 'Counsel in a man's heart is deep water, and a man of understanding draws it out' is read as a well whose water was cold and good but unreachable until someone tied rope to rope, thread to thread, cord to cord, and drew - so Judah answered on every single matter, not relenting, until he reached the heart. The mechanism behind the universality: each clause is a knot, and the depth is only reached by adding them. A model of argument as accumulation rather than as force.

check.note: Persuasion modelled as drawing water from a deep well by tying line to line, each clause of the speech a knot.

claim_en: A RIVAL TRANSLATOR IS NAMED AND WEIGHED INSIDE THE MIDRASH, BESIDE THE ONE THIS PROJECT READS. Explaining 'a word spoken ‹עַל אָפְנָיו› (al ofnav)' as words found sound on every side - like a WHEEL ‹אוֹפָן› ('ofan') showing its face all round - the passage cites AKILAS THE PROSELYTE's rival rendering of the verse by name. The chain is therefore recorded doing exactly what this project does: naming a translation, quoting it, and weighing it as evidence. The persuasion is measured by universality rather than by force, and the seam between the reading shelf and the testing shelf shows again.

check.note: A named rival translator quoted and weighed inside the midrash, beside the translation the reading declares.

claim_en: THE CONFESSION VERSE IS DEPERSONALIZED BY THE TRANSLATION EXACTLY WHERE THE CHAIN PERSONALIZES IT. 'GOD HAS FOUND the iniquity of your servants' becomes 'FROM BEFORE the LORD the iniquity of your servants HAS BEEN FOUND' - active turned passive, the finding removed from God's own hand. The standing reading of the identical clause goes the other way: the creditor has FOUND his occasion to collect the note. Two members of the declared reading pulling in opposite directions on one verb, and both are kept.

check.note: A confession clause turned passive by the translation at the same seat where the chain reads it as a creditor's active collection.

claim_en: A THREE-SPEECH LEDGER OPENED AT THE SALE CLOSES ON THIS UNIT'S INK, TWO OF THE THREE BEING HERE. The standing reading holds that three speeches crowned Judah king, and two of them are in this block - 'Judah and his brothers came' at 44:14 and 'Judah approached him' at 44:18 - the third being his proposal at the sale. Verified at the ink: all three verses stand as the reading names them, with the speaker named first in each. A kingship accounted for by speech acts, and the account completes here.

check.note: An enumerated three-speech ledger for a kingship, two of whose members stand in this unit's verses.

claim_en: A RENDING-REPAYMENT TABLE TAKES ITS FIRST INSTALLMENT AT THIS VERSE. The standing table holds that the brothers who caused their father to rend his garments would rend their own, and 44:13 is its first repayment - they rent their clothes when the goblet was found. A measure-for-measure ledger opened at the sale block and drawing here, on a verse whose plain sense is only distress.

check.note: A measure-for-measure table opened at an earlier block taking its first repayment at this verse.

claim_en: THE DUEL IS STAGED AS A TEST OF STRENGTH AND ENDS IN A RECOGNITION OF FEAR OF HEAVEN. Framed by 'wisdom fortifies the wise more than ten rulers in a city,' the confrontation is given a physical dossier: a roar carrying four hundred parsangs until a nephew leapt from Canaan to join it; both men roaring as lions until Egypt was near upended and the teeth of the warriors fell out; the brothers kicking the ground into furrows; Joseph kicking the stone pillar he sat on into a heap of pebbles. The signs of the rage are themselves disputed - blood from both eyes, or the single hair over the heart that tore through five garments of armor. And it resolves not by force but by a judgment: the sword would not leave its scabbard, and 'this one must be a God-fearing man.'

check.note: A physical confrontation dossier with its signs recorded as disputed, resolving in a recognition of piety rather than in violence.

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION SUPPLIES THE PREMISE THE WHOLE ARGUMENT RESTS ON, AND KEEPS THE PLEDGE IN ONE LEGAL WORD. 'His soul is BOUND UP ‹קְשׁוּרָה› (keshura) with his soul' becomes 'his soul is AS BELOVED TO HIM AS HIS OWN' - the binding idiom read as love, which is exactly the premise Judah's argument needs to work. Two verses later the pledge is rendered with the same technical suretyship term used at its original making, so the making and the invoking carry one legal word across the block seam - which is what the chain's whole proverb reading requires.

check.note: A binding idiom rendered as love, supplying the argument's premise, with the suretyship term held constant from pledge to invocation.

claim_en: THE UNIT ENDS MID-SPEECH, AND THE BREAK IS DECLARED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. This unit spans the whole of chapter 44, so it carries the opening seventeen verses of the next weekly portion - the speech - under the block-boundary law. The speech does not conclude here: it breaks off at 'Joseph could not restrain himself,' which opens the next unit at 45:1, still underived. The standing confrontation dossier likewise reaches past this boundary - the counter-question 'why not for your brother, when you sold him for twenty silver and told your father TORN, TORN,' and the count of twelve marketplaces with the threat to destroy three. The seam is recorded as an open edge, not closed.

check.note: A unit boundary that cuts a speech in mid-course, declared openly with the continuation named at the next unit's opening verse.

claim_en: THE FOUND-FOUND CHAIN'S FIRST LINK. The Passover leaven-search law rides a four-link verbal-analogy chain whose first link is this unit's goblet scene — searched, and it was found — the bridge the sweep predicted now read at its seat. Filed F-147, auto-seated (round 36, the name-and-ink block).
